content.comment_body: Hi, I'm trying to display the status images of two outputs, Q1 and Q2, in my message text. All other messages are shown correctly, but the I/O states appear only in the software simulation, not on the device screen.
Q1 and Q2 are OFF, so the display shows a 0 (zero). What do you expect to see when Q1 and/or Q2 are OFF, and what when they are ON? Please share your program.
You can use the I/O status names for this purpose. See the attached file.
Hi, I’ve uploaded a new image. I've already followed your suggestion, but it only works in the simulation, not on the device screen, and only for the I/O block. Very odd!
What exactly are you trying to achieve? How are the output and the counter supposed to interact?

I'm using the counter to track how many times Q1 and Q2 switch. There’s no issue with that, as I can see the count on the device screen. My problem is that I can't see the I/O status on the device screen, even though it works in the software.
Could you share your program? Then we can try it ourselves. What is the type and version of the device you’re using?
Here it is, you can rename it as lsc. I'm using [company_name] [product_name] [version_no] and expansion module [product_name].

I have downloaded your program into my device. The display in the device and simulation are identical. Could you provide a clearer description of your issue? I still don't understand what you're experiencing. Edit: What specifically do you see in the simulation that is missing on your device display? Is it the state of Q1 and Q2?
Exactly, I can't see the state of Q1 and Q2 on my device screen.

Directly displaying the status of a digital output in a message text isn’t possible. It can only be done indirectly via the I/O status name, bar graph, or as a number (0 or 1) using arithmetic instructions. Direct display is only available in the system menu.
Here’s a simple program that demonstrates the three options.
Hi, The display of the device has 6 lines and 16 cells per line. Since Q1 and Q2 begin at cell 17, they're not visible. See attachment.
Hello [user_name], In this case, it doesn’t matter because the ticker enables a line width of 32 characters.
Sorry for the blurry image, but as you can see, my device doesn’t show the I/O state. I’m not sure why it works on your device and not mine if the code is the same.

analysis.insight_summary: The user notices a difference between the simulation (software environment) and the actual device display: while the state of outputs Q1 and Q2 is visible in simulation, it is not shown on the device screen. Other message texts display correctly, suggesting a specific gap in real-time I/O status feedback on hardware compared to software.
analysis.user_expectations: The user expects their device screen to display the real-time status (on/off) of outputs Q1 and Q2, just as it does in the software simulation.
